sentences.text: The animal is known mainly from a single skull and thick skull roofs measuring 22 cm, with estimates of its length at 4.5 meters and weight between 370 and 450 kilograms.
Pachycephalosaurus was a bipedal herbivore with long strong legs and small five-fingered hands.
It possessed a large bony dome on its skull up to 25 cm thick that cushioned its brain.
The bony spikes on the snout were likely blunted rather than sharp.
Pachycephalosaurus wyomingensis is the only known species in the extinct genus Pachycephalosaurus.
This animal is a marginocephalian dinosaur belonging to the family Pachycephalosauridae.
It is the largest known pachycephalosaur, distinguished by an extremely thick, slightly domed skull roof.
Some estimates suggest it reached lengths of 4.5 to 5 meters and weighed up to 2000 kilograms.
Research found that 22% of examined domes had lesions consistent with osteomyelitis, supporting the use of domes in combat.
Fossils have been found in Montana, South Dakota, Wyoming, and Alberta.
American paleontologist Joseph Leidy named the taxon Tylosteus ornatus seventy-one years before Pachycephalosaurus was described, based on a bone fragment he interpreted as reptile armor.
A partial skull was discovered in 1930 by George Fryer Sternberg in the Lance Formation of Niobrara County, Wyoming.
The genus Pachycephalosaurus was established by Brown and Schlaikjer in 1943.
The skull structure suggests the animal used its dome as a battering ram for defense or intraspecific combat, similar to modern bighorn sheep or muskoxen.
A 2012 study suggested that cranial pathologies in a specimen were caused by aggressive behavior.
Histological examination reveals that domes are made of fibrolamellar bone containing fibroblasts critical for wound healing.
Research by Cary Woodruff noted that the spine, pelvis, and tail resemble those of kangaroos rather than head-butting animals.
The animal had very small, ridged teeth that were ineffective for chewing tough, fibrous plants.
The most complete fossil jaw shows serrated, blade-like front teeth reminiscent of carnivorous theropods.
It was a bipedal, possibly omnivorous dinosaur with an extremely thick skull roof.
It is suspected that the dinosaur may have included meat in its diet.
Pachycephalosaurus names the clade Pachycephalosauria, a group of herbivorous ornithischian dinosaurs from the Late Cretaceous of North America and Asia.
In 2009, Horenr and Goodwin proposed that Stygimoloch and Dracorex are juvenile growth stages of Pachycephalosaurus and should be classified as synonyms.
In 2007, researchers proposed that related genera Stygimoloch and Dracorex were juvenile or female forms of Pachycephalosaurus.
The genus Tylosteus is considered synonymous with Pachycephalosaurus.
The animal lived during the Maastrichtian age of the Late Cretaceous period in western North America, shortly before the Cretaceous–Paleogene extinction event.
It lived during the Late Cretaceous, specifically the Maastrichtian stage, between 68 and 66 million years ago.
It coexisted with diverse dinosaurs including ceratopsians, ankylosaurids, nodosaurids, and theropods like Tyrannosaurus.
The hypothesis that Pachycephalosaurus used its skull dome for head-butting has been disputed in recent years.
In 1990, W. P. Coombs suggested a tooth found by Hatcher came from a pachycephalosaurid, possibly Pachycephalosaurus.
It is debated whether Pachycephalosaurus used its dome for head-butting like bighorn sheep or for flank-butting like kangaroos.
